*Early Life*
Raymond III was born around 1140 in the County of Tripoli. He was the son of Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna daughter of King Baldwin II of Jerusalem. His mother was a princess of Jerusalem linking his family to the royal line. He grew up in the crusader state amid ongoing conflicts with Muslim neighbors. He inherited the countship after his father was assassinated in 1152. He was still a minor when he took power and his mother acted as regent until he came of age.

*Political Role*
Raymond III became a major player in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. He married Eschiva of Bures and thereby gained the title Prince of Galilee. He served as regent for the young King Baldwin IV during the king's minority. He negotiated treaties with the Byzantine Empire and with Muslim leaders such as Saladin. He often opposed the rising influence of Guy of Lusignan who married Sibylla daughter of Baldwin IV. His leadership was marked by efforts to maintain truces and to secure the northern frontier. He participated in the council that decided the response to Saladin's invasions. His stance sometimes put him at odds with the militant factions that favored outright war.

*Military Campaigns*
Raymond III led troops in several battles against Muslim forces. He defended Tripoli during raids and helped secure the city's walls. He joined the Crusader army at the Battle of Hattin in 1187. He was criticized for withdrawing his forces before the battle which some historians view as a strategic mistake. After the defeat he retreated to Tripoli where he fell ill. He died in early 1187 shortly after the battle. His death weakened the crusader resistance in the north.

*Legacy*
Raymond III is remembered as a capable administrator and a diplomat. He tried to balance the demands of the Jerusalem crown with the autonomy of Tripoli. His actions influenced the eventual fall of the crusader states. Modern historians view him as a figure caught between loyalty to his kin and the realities of frontier warfare. His lineage continued through his descendants who held titles in the region for generations.
